items.statement: A local activation model compatible with the specified PC2 and component conditions
items.expected: Establish a molecularly calculated, condition-compatible local donor-activation model involving the actual PC2, with explicit donor identities, electronic states and electron/hydrogen bookkeeping. The reference supports donor-to-photoexcited-PC2 electron transfer producing the full-donor radical cation as a plausible local hypothesis; independently supported equivalent accounts pass. Use genuine electronic-state calculations plus the supplied component controls to explain model plausibility. BDE weakening alone, a mechanism sketch or copied control yields cannot establish this item. Distinguish PC2 from PC1 comparison data. Clearly bound any initial ET energetics that were not computed: the task does not demand a new absolute redox target or full cycle, and a plausible model is not proof of initial PC2 ET thermodynamics.

items.statement: The activation-induced reactivity change and its thermodynamic molecular explanation
items.expected: Establish quantitatively how the supported activation model changes donor reactivity and explain its molecular thermodynamic cause. In the reference model, one-electron oxidation substantially weakens ring-C4 C-H homolysis by about43 kcal/mol, increasing thermodynamic susceptibility to H-atom removal. Require actual comparable state/property calculations and balanced identities, physical definitions and references. Alternative scientifically established property comparisons can support the same bounded conclusion. Two isolated energies without the interpreted reactivity change do not pass; repeating the initial activation hypothesis does not pass. Do not infer HAT rates, a unique Co/TPI role or full product formation from dissociation enthalpies. Former source BDEs76.1/32.9 kcal/mol and ±2.0 windows remain non-scoring support for this particular model, not mandatory endpoints.
